title: Syed
body:
Q: What is Java?
Ans: Java is a high-level, object-oriented, platform-independent programming language which achieves platform independence using bytecode and JVM.
• Here high level means the language which is easy to read and write also hide hardware level details

Q: What is the difference between JDK, JRE, and JVM?
Ans:
• JDK: JDK is a complete package required to develop Java applications. It contains JRE + Development Tools (like javac, debugger).
• JRE: Environment for running applications (includes libraries and JVM).
• JVM: JVM is a virtual machine like minicomputer that executes Java bytecode then JVM use interpreter to execute bytecode line by line to machine code. Before that compiler convert source code to bytecode.

Q: What is a compiler and an interpreter?
Ans: The compiler converts Java source code into bytecode also A compiler translates the entire code at once (faster execution), Interpreter executes bytecode line by line also interpreter translates line-by-line (easier debugging). Java uses a compiler to create bytecode and the JVM to interpret/compile it at runtime.

Q: Is the JIT compiler different from the regular compiler?
Ans: Yes. The regular compiler (javac) creates bytecode before execution. The Just-In-Time (JIT) compiler converts bytecode to native machine code during runtime to improve performance.

Q: Explain Java's platform independence.
Ans: Java compiles source code into platform-neutral bytecode (.class files). Any system with a JVM can execute this bytecode, regardless of the underlying hardware or OS.

Q: What is bytecode in Java?
Ans: Bytecode is a machine-independent instruction set contained in .class files. It serves as the intermediate step between Java source code and machine-specific code, executed only by the JVM.

Q: OOPS concepts?
Ans
• Encapsulation: Imagine you have a Diary with a lock on it. It hides the internal data and only allows access through public methods.
• Inheritance: Imagine a Super-Class called Phone. All phones can make calls, and child classes like SmartPhone inherit these features.
• Polymorphism: Polymorphism is a big word that just means Many Shapes. It allows methods to do different things based on the object (Overloading/Overriding).
• Abstraction: When you want a cup of coffee from a vending machine, you just press the button that says Cocoa. You don't need to know how the machine mixes it internally.

Q: Other OOPS concepts?
Ans
• Association, Aggregation, and Composition: These define the 'has-a' relationship between objects, varying by how strongly the objects are tied to each other's lifecycle.

Q:Java 8 features?
Ans
• Lambda Expressions, Stream API, Functional Interfaces, Optional Class, and Default/Static methods in Interfaces.

Q:Java 21 features?
Ans
• Virtual Threads (Project Loom), Sequenced Collections, Record Patterns, and String Templates (Preview).

Q:Java memory management?
Ans
• Java memory is divided into Heap (objects) and Stack (method execution/references). Garbage Collection automatically reclaims unused heap memory.

Q:Kafka?
Ans
• Apache Kafka is a distributed event streaming platform used for high-performance data pipelines, streaming analytics, and data integration.

Q:What is JDBC?
Ans
• JDBC (Java Database Connectivity) is an API that allows Java applications to interact with databases using SQL queries.

Q:What is Threads?
Ans
• A thread is a lightweight subprocess, the smallest unit of processing. Multithreading allows concurrent execution of two or more parts of a program.
